Greater
Manchester, like the rest of the country, is facing significant
fostering sufficiency challenges. There are fewer mainstream
fostering placements available than six years ago, while demand for
children’s care placements has continued to grow. This has
contributed to greater reliance on residential care, independent
provision and placements that may be further from children’s
families, schools and communities.
The GM Fostering Hub was established to strengthen
recruitment through a shared regional approach to marketing,
enquiry handling and early applicant engagement. The Hub has
improved visibility of fostering across Greater Manchester,
strengthened early-stage conversion and created a more consistent
experience for people interested in fostering. The next phase is
about building on that foundation so the Hub can support the whole
journey from initial interest through assessment, approval and
early support.
Greater Manchester’s approach is to build an end-to-end
hub that is regional in design, locally connected and aligned to
the wider GM sufficiency programme. Local authorities will continue
to retain statutory responsibility for children, placement
decisions and their wider fostering duties, while the Hub will
increasingly provide a shared route for recruitment, assessment,
approval and early support.
